facts.fact: The Ministry of Local Government's annual report for 2024-2025 says its Land Use Planning Unit coordinates with the Economic Development Board and the local authorities on the National Electronic Licensing System for processing Building and Land Use Permit applications, and reports that the local authorities received 24,958 such applications and approved 13,453 between 1 July 2024 and 30 June 2025.

The Ministry's table of Building and Land Use Permit applications for 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025 lists all 12 local authorities (one municipal city council, four municipal town councils, seven district councils) of the 12 the report says the country has; the report names the National Electronic Licensing System as the system for processing these applications but does not itself say the table's figures passed through it or where the staff work.

systems.owner: coordinated by the Ministry's Land Use Planning Unit with the Economic Development Board
systems.tiers: local authorities, for Building and Land Use Permit applications; also the Mauritius Fire and Rescue Service, for online fire certificate applications and inspection reports
complaints on community services: of 12,000 received through the portal, 6,600 (55%) addressed as at 30 June 2025, against a target of 72%, as the Ministry's outcome indicator for local communities
named only as a launch attended by 2 Ministry officers in 2024-2025; no description

note: Excerpt: the captured text stops at Annex 6.2, before any staffing table. Both facts rest on the study's rule that working in a national system held elsewhere states a connection; the report never mentions a network, a line or internet at council offices, which the parent should weigh. It also records that market visits found a need for digital payment systems, and names no local authority ICT budget line.
